newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian stocks seen rebounding after turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian stocks seen rebounding after turmoil.

text.p: Sound economic fundamentals will provide a springboard for a rebound in Indonesia's stock market which has shadowed a slide in the local currency, the rupiah, analysts said on Friday.

Jakarta stocks plunged to a year-low in afternoon trade on Friday, with the composite index down about 3.4 percent at 621 points at 0810 GMT as the rupiah plunged to new depths against the U.S. dollar.

"There are expectations that investors will come back (into the market) sooner than any other country in the region and I am very confident that the market turnaround will be quite strong," said Gunawan Jusuf, managing director of local brokerage Makindo Securities.

"The analysis so far has been that because of the government's prudent and consistent policies, macro-economic stability is quite solid," he told Reuters on the sidelines of an international capital market conference in Jakarta.

Friday's stock plunge was one in a series of falls the index has suffered since offshore speculative attacks on the rupiah and other regional currencies led to higher interest rates. The stock index hit a lifetime high of 742.95 points on July 9.
I. Putu Gede Ary Suta, chairman of the capital market supervisory agency, took the declines in stride, saying that the rupiah's decline posed no long-term problems to stocks.
"I think we don't have a problem with this because our economic fundamentals are good," he told Reuters. "When we have a good economy, the capital market will be good."
"I believe this is temporary and will be no problem for us. As regulators we want to make sure the system is in place and the market mechanism is working," he added.

Financial expert Marshall Loeb, a former managing editor of Fortune magazine, told the conference Indonesia had an "excellent" record of economic growth and investors from around the world would be looking to invest in the archipelago.

"The opportunity is there, surely, to get not so much more in the way of direct investment in specific Indonesian shares but to get Indonesia as part of various global and pan-Asian mutual funds," he said during his presentation.
Makindo's Gunawan said it was unavoidable for Indonesia to feel the contagion effect of regional markets, which in recent weeks had been suffering from their currencies' volatility.

"In general, people will go back to fundamental evaluation, with macro-economic policy taking top place," he said, adding that investors would be coming back to the Indonesian stock market with an eye on strategic and undervalued sectors.
He said the central bank's decision to scrap the rupiah intervention band and free-float the currency was just one indication of how the government was ahead of the market.

"The government has now let the market decide and test it (the rupiah). They (the government) know it will overshoot or undershoot, but in the end the market will find an equilibrium and after that they (investors) will come in," he said.
"The market feels a big relief. It (scrapping of the band) is positive for the market, which will improve in the next few weeks," he said.
